methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses an appropriately labeled feasibility design (Section 2.1) with LOOCV to accommodate a very small single-center retrospective cohort (n=44 after exclusions from 82). Feature selection combines Brunner–Munzel filtering, Spearman redundancy pruning, VIF multicollinearity control (threshold 10), and LASSO (Section 2.6.2), and XGBoost hyperparameters are tuned by nested 5x5-fold CV with fixed seeds — reasonable choices. However, the ratio of 93 dosiomic + 36 DVH candidate features to 44 patients, with SMOTE and feature selection, raises overfitting concerns; it is unclear whether SMOTE and the inner tuning were applied strictly inside each LOOCV fold or on the full dataset, which could inflate performance. Toxicity grading was performed by a single radiation oncologist (K.Y.) with no inter-rater reliability data (Section 2.2), three different TPS were pooled without harmonization (acknowledged), and no external validation is performed. DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction for intra- and inter-OAR AUC comparisons are appropriate (Section 2.7), confidence intervals are reported, but no a priori power/sample-size justification is provided.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective, single-center series of 44 patients used to derive and internally cross-validate a prognostic/prediction model (Section 2.2–2.6), which maps to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort / case series). The clinical question — predicting acute xerostomia and dysphagia to guide treatment planning and toxicity management — is clinically meaningful, and endpoints are patient-centered (CTCAE grade 2+ xerostomia/dysphagia within 90 days). However, with no external validation, no demonstration that predictions change planning decisions or outcomes, limited sample size, and inconsistent gains over DVH for xerostomia (per-gland AUCs 0.26–0.61 in the discussion), the translational path remains preliminary. The authors themselves frame it as feasibility and note generalizability must be established.

reporting_quality.justification: Because this is development and internal validation of a prediction model for toxicity classification, TRIPOD is the appropriate checklist. Many TRIPOD items are addressed: source of data, participant eligibility, outcome definition (CTCAE v5 binarized at grade 2), candidate predictors, feature selection, model specification (XGBoost with listed hyperparameter grid), internal validation (LOOCV), performance metrics (AUC with 95% CI, sensitivity, specificity), and some discussion of limitations. Gaps include no explicit TRIPOD declaration, no calibration assessment, no reporting of a full prediction equation or deployable model, no handling-of-missing-data statement, limited sample-size justification, a single assessor for the outcome without reliability data, and no reporting flow diagram. Data availability is weak: supplementary methods and tables are referenced (Method S1/S2, Table S1–S3) but there is no mention of a public repository for data or code, nor any accession/DOI.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is empirical/population-level: this is plausibly the first dosiomics study to apply the approach systematically to acute dysphagia across multiple swallowing-related OARs (superior/middle/inferior PCM, cricopharyngeal, supra/glottic larynx), and the first to incorporate oral cavity minor salivary glands rather than only parotid/submandibular glands for xerostomia dosiomics. The positioning versus prior xerostomia dosiomics work (Gabryś, Abdollahi, Zhang) and classical dysphagia DVH/ML models (Dean, Mazzola, Alterio) is adequately described. However, both the methodology (XGBoost on PyRadiomics-style features) and the broader concept (dosiomics for radiation toxicity) are well-established, so the contribution is a meaningful but incremental extension rather than a conceptual or methodological breakthrough.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and logically organized: introduction motivates the gap in multi-OAR dosiomics, methods walk through the pipeline in order, and discussion engages prior literature per endpoint. Acronyms (HNC, OAR, DVH, PCM, LOOCV) are generally expanded on first use, and the abstract is quantitatively grounded with AUCs and CIs. Weaknesses include a duplicative two-part abstract (narrative paragraph followed by Background/Methods/Results/Conclusions), occasional awkward phrasing ('demonstrating the feasibility'), overuse of hedging in the discussion, and heavy reliance on supplementary tables for crucial parameters. Figures and tables are referenced but captions are not evaluable in this format.

key_strengths: Clear feasibility framing with explicit acknowledgment of sample-size limits (n=44) and single-center scope
Reasonable modeling pipeline: multi-step feature selection (Brunner–Munzel → Spearman → VIF ≤10 → LASSO), XGBoost tuning with fixed seeds, LOOCV, and DeLong AUC comparisons with Bonferroni correction
Novel inclusion of oral cavity and multiple swallowing OARs rather than only parotid/submandibular glands, extending dosiomics beyond prior xerostomia-only work
Clinically meaningful endpoints (CTCAE v5 grade ≥2 acute xerostomia and dysphagia) with best AUCs of 0.843 (xerostomia, all OARs) and 0.878 (dysphagia, middle PCM)
key_concerns: Very small single-center cohort (44 patients) combined with ~129 candidate features, SMOTE, and internal CV only — high overfitting risk and no external validation
Single-rater toxicity grading with no inter-rater reliability; outcome is subject to assessor variability
Ambiguity about whether SMOTE and inner hyperparameter tuning were strictly nested within each LOOCV fold, which affects performance validity
TRIPOD items incompletely addressed: no calibration, no missing-data handling statement, no deployable model equation, no participant-flow diagram
No data or code availability statement; three different TPS pooled without harmonization (acknowledged but not corrected)
Negative/null findings for parotid and submandibular glands (AUCs 0.26–0.61) contradict established dosimetric knowledge, hinting at analytic instability rather than a true biological signal
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent but highly preliminary single-center feasibility study with meaningful but incremental novelty, limited sample size, and no external validation. It is best suited to a Tier 4 oncology/medical-physics journal with minor revisions clarifying nested CV, adding reporting-standard adherence, and strengthening data/code availability.
